summary: Revision round 3 (attempt 2): the only open finding, SEC-10, cannot be fixed without changing back-end/ShipRight.Server/Modules/Projects/ProjectRouter.cs, which the design scope does not include (for that module it lists Modules/Projects/MariadbProjectStore.cs only). GET /api/projects (ProjectRouter.cs:16-17) and GET /api/projects/{id} (lines 33-39) return ProjectConfig whole, so DockerPassword (ProjectConfig.cs:48) and database RootPassword (ProjectConfig.cs:18) reach Viewer and Operator callers: RoleAccessRules.cs has no /api/projects GET rule, so the default at line 73 makes both Viewer (asserted by RoleAccessRulesTests.cs:31). The reviewer's prescribed fix - blank those fields for non-Admin, as the team/password responses do - needs the endpoint, which alone knows the caller's role and can return a role-shaped DTO. No in-scope fix works: raising the rule to Admin in Modules/Identity/RoleAccessRules.cs would stop a Viewer listing projects, which R5 requires, and redacting in the company-scoped store (CompanyScopedProjectStore, MariadbProjectStore.cs:149) would break the internal consumers that legitimately need the credentials (BuildOrchestrator.cs:755/1130, ResourceResolutionService.cs:39) and the credential-preserving save path. Per the ground rules I changed no code and filed a scope kickback citing R5. The same 244 tests from the previous round are reported unchanged.

kickbacks.reason: SEC-10 needs GET /api/projects and GET /api/projects/{id} to stop returning DockerPassword and database RootPassword to non-Admin callers (blank them as the team/password responses do) while R5 still requires a Viewer to be able to list projects, so the response has to be shaped per the caller's role. Both endpoints, and the only place that knows the signed-in role, are in ProjectRouter.cs (lines 16-17 and 33-39), which the design scope omits (it lists Modules/Projects/MariadbProjectStore.cs but not ProjectRouter.cs). No in-scope alternative exists: raising the /api/projects GET rule to Admin in Modules/Identity/RoleAccessRules.cs would stop a Viewer listing projects (breaking R5 and RoleAccessRulesTests.cs:31), and blanking the secrets in the company-scoped store (CompanyScopedProjectStore, Modules/Projects/MariadbProjectStore.cs:149) would break the internal consumers that legitimately need them (BuildOrchestrator.cs:755/1130, ResourceResolutionService.cs:39) and the credential-preserving save path. ProjectRouter.cs needs to be added to the design scope.
